report_name: 19 Malicious Chrome & Edge Extensions Caught Stealing Crypto Wallets

attack_patterns.name: Software Extensions
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors published 19 malicious browser extensions for Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge to steal cryptocurrency and credentials. This was used for initial access and persistence within the user's browser.

attack_patterns.name: Browser Session Hijacking
attack_patterns.description: The malicious extensions removed a website's Content Security Policy (CSP) headers, allowing the injection of arbitrary malicious JavaScript into any webpage the user visited to steal data.

attack_patterns.name: Protocol Tunneling
attack_patterns.description: The extensions established a persistent WebSocket connection to a C2 server for real-time, bidirectional communication to exfiltrate stolen data and receive new commands.

attack_patterns.name: Keylogging
attack_patterns.description: Injected scripts were used to capture form data as it was entered by the user on various websites, including cryptocurrency exchanges.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
attack_patterns.description: The malware included modules for stealing Facebook and LinkedIn session cookies to take over active user sessions.

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
attack_patterns.description: Attackers compromised the supply chain by pushing malicious updates to existing, trusted browser extensions, turning them into malware against their user base.

attack_patterns.name: Web Portal Capture
attack_patterns.description: The malware presented fake recovery pages mimicking Ledger and Trezor hardware wallet interfaces to harvest seed phrases from users.

malware.name: Superior
malware.description: A modular malware framework distributed via browser extensions, designed to steal cryptocurrency wallet secrets, hardware wallet seed phrases, and credentials for crypto exchanges and social media sites.

malware.name: Enable Right Click & Copy — Smart Unlock + OCR
malware.description: The most popular malicious browser extension in the 'Superior' campaign, which had approximately 80,000 users and was used to deliver wallet-draining and credential-stealing payloads.

campaigns.name: Superior
campaigns.description: A large-scale malware campaign active since at least February 2024, involving 19 malicious browser extensions for Chrome and Edge designed to steal cryptocurrency assets and user credentials.
campaigns.objective: Steal cryptocurrency assets, wallet seed phrases, and user credentials for financial gain.

identities.name: Ledger
identities.description: A hardware wallet vendor whose interface was mimicked by the malware to trick users into revealing their seed phrases.

identities.name: Trezor
identities.description: A hardware wallet vendor whose interface was mimicked by the malware to trick users into revealing their seed phrases.

identities.name: Binance
identities.description: A major cryptocurrency exchange whose user credentials were targeted for theft by the malicious extensions.

identities.name: Coinbase
identities.description: A major cryptocurrency exchange whose user credentials were targeted for theft by the malicious extensions.

identities.name: Kraken
identities.description: A major cryptocurrency exchange whose user credentials were targeted for theft by the malicious extensions.

identities.name: Facebook
identities.description: A social media platform whose user session cookies were targeted for theft by the malware.

identities.name: LinkedIn
identities.description: A professional networking platform whose user session cookies were targeted for theft by the malware.

infrastructure.name: Superior C2 Server
infrastructure.description: Command and control server that communicated with the malicious browser extensions via a persistent WebSocket connection to exfiltrate data and deliver payloads.

observables.name: Enable Right Click & Copy — Smart Unlock + OCR

indicators.name: Malicious Extension 'Enable Right Click & Copy' Detection
indicators.stix_pattern: [file:name = 'Enable Right Click & Copy — Smart Unlock + OCR']
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Malicious Chrome Extension 'Enable Right Click & Copy' Installation
id: 7e8c9d0a-1b2c-4d5e-8f9a-0b1c2d3e4f5a
status: experimental
description: Detects the installation of the malicious 'Enable Right Click & Copy — Smart Unlock + OCR' browser extension by looking for its name in file creation events within browser extension directories.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-31
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/19-chrome-and-edge-extensions-found.html
tags:
  - attack.t1176
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Extensions\'
      - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\Default\Extensions\'
    TargetFilename|endswith: 'Enable Right Click & Copy — Smart Unlock + OCR'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the presence of the named malicious browser extension 'Enable Right Click & Copy — Smart Unlock + OCR'.

indicators.name: Suspicious Persistent WebSocket Connection from Browser
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Persistent WebSocket Connection from Browser
id: f1a2b3c4-d5e6-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects persistent WebSocket connections from Chrome or Edge browsers, which could indicate a malicious extension maintaining a C2 channel.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-31
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/19-chrome-and-edge-extensions-found.html
tags:
  - attack.t1572
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
    Protocol: 'tcp'
    Initiated: true
  filter_known_good:
    DestinationHostname|endswith:
      - '.google.com'
      - '.microsoft.com'
      - '.live.com'
  condition: selection and not filter_known_good
indicators.description: Detects persistent WebSocket connections from browser processes, a technique used by the 'Superior' malware for C2 communication.

indicators.name: Browser Extension File Modification
indicators.pattern:
title: Browser Extension File Modification
id: 1234abcd-efgh-4ijk-lmno-pqrstuvwxyza
status: experimental
description: Monitors for file creation or modification in browser extension directories, which could indicate the installation of a new or updated malicious extension.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-31
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/19-chrome-and-edge-extensions-found.html
tags:
  - attack.t1176
level: low
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Extensions\'
      - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\Default\Extensions\'
      - '/.config/google-chrome/Default/Extensions/'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation or modification of files within browser extension directories, a hunting hint provided in the article.
